title: Claude Cowork
content:
## Overview

**Cowork** is Anthropic's agentic harness for general knowledge work — the same background-agent model that powers Claude Code's scheduled and remote sessions, but aimed at non-coding tasks. Anthropic has said more than 90% of Cowork usage is not software work: it's used for research, report building, data aggregation, and other multi-step office tasks that used to require constant supervision.

---

## Mobile and Web Expansion (July 7, 2026)

Cowork originally launched as a desktop-tethered feature. On July 7, 2026, Anthropic expanded it to web and mobile, so a session's files and progress follow the user across devices instead of staying locked to one machine:

- **Web:** Cowork sessions launch directly from the claude.ai home screen.
- **Mobile:** available in the sidebar of Claude's iOS and Android apps, with **mobile approvals** — a user can review and approve a pending agent action from their phone without opening a laptop.
- **Background execution:** work continues in the cloud even after a laptop is closed or goes offline. Scheduled tasks, data aggregation, and report generation keep running autonomously rather than pausing when the initiating device disconnects.

The rollout began in beta for Max subscribers, with wider availability planned in the following weeks.

---

## How It Relates to Claude Code

Cowork and Claude Code's remote/scheduled sessions share the same underlying execution model described in the Claude Code Overview page: an isolated cloud container is spun up, the agent works with full tool access, and results are only durable once committed/saved somewhere outside the container. The distinguishing feature of Cowork is that it's positioned for the rest of the office, not just engineering — the equivalent of a coding agent's "PR-and-CI" loop, but for spreadsheets, documents, and research briefs.

Subsequent July 2026 updates broadened the same surface: Cowork sessions gained shared chat and projects for Team/Enterprise use, and Claude Code separately shipped **live MCP connector data for published Artifacts** — an artifact can now call an MCP connector each time it's viewed, so a dashboard shows current data (and can take actions on demand) instead of a frozen snapshot from when the session built it.

---

## Practical Implications

- **Approvals matter more, not less.** Because work can execute unattended in the background, the mobile approval step is the main safety checkpoint — treat approval prompts as real decision points, not rubber stamps.
- **State lives in the session's outputs, not the device.** As with any remote/background agent session, anything not saved to a persistent store (a file committed to a repo, a document saved to Drive, etc.) can be lost when a session ends.
- **Scheduling and background work compose.** A Cowork session can be the mechanism behind a recurring scheduled task (like this wiki maintenance agent), running on its own cadence and only surfacing to a human when something needs a decision.
